title: What Is It Made Of?
subtitle: Grade 1 Science
objectives: Identify, name, describe, sort and group common materials, including wood, plastic, metal, glass, rock, paper and fabric.
Understand the difference between an object and a material.
Understand that all materials have a variety of properties.
Describe common materials in terms of their properties.
Describe how materials can be changed by physical action, e.g. stretching, compressing, bending and twisting.
Talk about how science explains how objects they use, or know about, work.

beats.say: Everything around you is made from a material.
A spoon, a chair, a window. What is each one made of?

at.what: What is each one made of?

beats.say: A spoon is an object. An object is a thing you can point at.
The spoon is made of metal. Metal is the material.
A chair is an object too. It is made of wood.
The object is the thing. The material is what it is made of.
Is the spoon made of spoon? No. Spoon is what it is. It is made of metal.
One material can make many objects. Wood makes chairs, pencils and doors.
Wood, metal, plastic, glass, rock, paper and fabric.
These are seven materials you see every day.
Outside science, material often means cloth. In science, it means anything a thing is made of.

at.anything: anything a thing is made of

beats.say: Look around the room. Almost everything you see is made of one of these seven.
Scientists test materials. Each test tells you a property.
Press it. Is it hard or soft? The sponge squashes, so it is soft.
Bend it. Does it bend or break? The sponge bends.
Wet it. Does the water go through? The sponge soaks it up.
Now test a metal spoon. It is hard, stiff and waterproof.
Every material has lots of properties at once.
Squash it, bend it, twist it, stretch it. Some materials change shape.
Push on clay and it squashes. Bend it, and it bends.
Pull an elastic band and it stretches. Twist it round and round.
Push on a stone and nothing happens. It keeps its shape.
Some materials change shape, and some do not.

scenes.heading: The right material for the job

beats.say: People choose a material because of its properties. That is science, used every day.
A window is glass because you can see through it.
A raincoat is plastic because water runs off it.
A paper raincoat? Paper soaks up water, so you would get wet.
The right material has the right properties for the job.
An object is a thing. A material is what it is made of.
You know seven materials, and tests find their properties.
Some materials change shape when you push or pull them.
Choose the right material for the job. Now go on a material hunt!
